purpose: Human-browsable canonical subject organization. These files are lightweight manifests/records; bulk corpus and indexes remain local/rebuildable.

characters.description: Named people and individual sapient beings.

deities.description: Gods, Daedra, culture-specific divinities and explicitly divine identities.

peoples.description: Races, cultures, peoples, species and collective beings.

locations.description: Continents, provinces, cities, ruins, realms and planes.

events.description: Wars, crises, migrations, disasters and other historical events.

organizations.description: Factions, dynasties, cults, orders, houses and political organizations.

religions.description: Religious systems, cult traditions and institutional doctrines.

artifacts.description: Named artifacts and important unique objects.

texts.description: In-universe works and their game-specific appearances.

concepts.description: Ideas, metaphysical concepts, titles, practices and notable substances.

structures.description: Important constructed structures when structure identity is more useful than geographic identity.

other.description: Temporary holding category for types awaiting normalization.

rules: Every subject has one primary directory for human browsing.
Cross-category identity is represented by relationships/aliases rather than duplicate canonical subject records.
Continuity and provenance are properties of claims/evidence, not directory names.
Game-specific appearances of a work may live under texts/appearances while the abstract work remains under texts.
Do not store fetched article bodies in Git; subject records point to local/rebuildable evidence.
New entity types must be mapped here before bulk ingestion.
